description: We’re Ángel and Diego, builders of MARS-NAV: a working web app that plans safe Marswalks with layered maps, hazard scoring, live Martian telemetry and a 3D rover simulation. We love space, code and data. Join us to power it with real NASA data! Looking for: GIS/remote sensing, machine learning (AI4Mars), 3D/WebGL, UX design and storytelling.
summary:
MARS-NAV: Safe Navigation and Exploration Planning on Mars

MARS-NAV is an interactive web application designed to help future explorers plan safer journeys across the Martian surface. It combines a layered planetary map with real NASA Mars Trek (JPL) orbital imagery and official USGS–NASA geological data, allowing users to explore Mars in both 2D and 3D.

The application features a risk-aware route planner that calculates lower-risk paths, a safe-zone finder that identifies potential shelter locations, and a telemetry system that estimates environmental conditions such as temperature, atmospheric pressure, gravity, radiation, wind, and dust. It also provides hazard assessments, geological information, distance and travel-time calculations, resource estimates, and a 3D simulation featuring a Perseverance-style rover and an astronaut.

MARS-NAV addresses the challenges of human exploration on Mars by transforming scientific planetary data into practical tools for mission planning and decision-making. Its goal is to help explorers better understand their surroundings, anticipate potential hazards, manage resources, and make more informed decisions, contributing to safer and more effective future Mars missions.
details:
MARS-NAV is an interactive web-based Mars exploration and mission-planning tool designed to help future astronauts plan safer Marswalks while identifying scientifically valuable locations.

The application combines real NASA orbital imagery from Mars Trek (JPL) with the official USGS–NASA Geologic Map of Mars (SIM 3292). Users can explore the Martian surface through a layered 2D map and a 3D planetary globe, switching between different orbital datasets, including Viking, MOLA, THEMIS, and CTX imagery.

Its main features include a route planner that calculates lower-cost paths using Dijkstra's algorithm across a terrain-cost grid, a safe-zone finder that evaluates potential shelter locations, and an environmental telemetry system that estimates temperature, atmospheric pressure, gravity, radiation, wind, and dust conditions. A decision panel provides hazard assessments, geological information, estimated travel times, resource requirements, and GO / CAUTION / NO-GO recommendations. The application also includes a 3D simulation featuring a rover, an astronaut, and interactive mission controls.

MARS-NAV was developed as a single-file web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Leaflet for 2D mapping and Three.js for 3D visualization. It directly integrates NASA map tiles and USGS geological vector data through web services.

Its creative approach combines planetary science, geographic visualization, route optimization, environmental modeling, and interactive simulation into one accessible interface. The project aims to make complex scientific data easier to understand and use, supporting better-informed decisions for future human exploration of Mars.

The team also considered important technical limitations: the 3D terrain is procedurally generated, environmental values are estimates, and calculated routes are not certified as safe. These limitations are explicitly communicated within the project.
